key_insight: LLMs labeled incidental findings in lung cancer screening CT reports with moderate to almost perfect agreement, but no model–prompt combination led across all nine findings.
clinical_relevance: This report-labeling research—not cancer drug discovery—could support identification of incidental findings for research and screening-program review.
method: Retrospective analysis of 300 CT reports from one Dutch academic hospital.
Compared four LLMs using four prompting strategies each, plus keyword-based search, against radiologist labels.
Assessed nine incidental findings using Cohen’s kappa, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores.
evidence_signal: GPT-5 achieved kappa values of 0.71–0.97 for seven findings; the highest reported agreement for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass was moderate (0.48 and 0.42, respectively).
watch_item: Single-center results require external validation, and variable performance across findings argues against assuming one model–prompt combination is universally reliable.
paper_title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
